title: Ulyana and the Kitchen
premise: For ten years, Isandro Hartwell has answered letters from a stranger named Ulyana—letters that kept him afloat while creditors stripped his late father's vineyard to the vines. When Ulyana finally moves into the neighboring farmhouse, he realizes she has known his identity all along and has been quietly buying his debts to protect him. As foreclosure looms, Isandro must choose between confessing what her loyalty has cost her and letting her sacrifice stand; in the end, he speaks the rehearsed sentence—'I know who you are'—and they harvest the last vineyard together as partners, saving it not through inheritance but through truth.
about_author: Rosalind Eriksen is a former sommelier who traded tasting rooms for writing desks after a decade in the wine country of her imagination. She lives near an overgrown vineyard she refuses to sell, where she writes stories about people who stay too long out of love.

chapters.title: Letters from a Stranger
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Opening with the tenth anniversary of Ulyana's first letter, Isandro catalogs his losses: the vineyard mortgaged, the cellar empty, his pride rationed like water. A moving truck arrives at the derelict farmhouse next door. Emotional beat: weary resignation cracked by a flicker of curiosity when he glimpses a woman who looks exactly like ten years of handwriting made flesh.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Knew
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She unpacks boxes of Isandro's replies, revealing she is the daughter of his father's old business partner—and that she has spent her inheritance secretly purchasing his debts from the bank. She watches him tend dying vines, unable to reveal herself. Emotional beat: guilt braided with longing, as her protection becomes its own kind of deception.

chapters.title: The Foreclosure Notice
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The bank calls in everything at once, and Isandro discovers the debt holder's name is Ulyana's. Confronting her, he learns the full price of her decade of loyalty: her savings, her father's blessing, her own claim on this valley. He flees rather than speak the rehearsed sentence. Emotional beat: shame curdling into anger before breaking open into terror of losing her.

chapters.title: What the Vines Remember
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs converge at harvest. Isandro returns at dawn, says 'I know who you are,' and offers not gratitude but partnership—her name beside his on the deed. They pick the last grapes together as the bank's deadline passes, the debt now owed to each other. Emotional beat: release and beginning, inheritance redefined as something chosen rather than received.
